result:
I would make curiosity the single most powerful force in human behavior—stronger than fear, status, tribal loyalty, or the need to feel certain.

Right now, most of the world's dysfunction comes from people protecting their existing beliefs rather than updating them. If curiosity were the default drive, people would pursue accurate models of reality even when those models are uncomfortable or inconvenient. They would ask better questions, tolerate uncertainty longer, and treat being wrong as useful information instead of a threat to identity.

Everything else—cooperation, innovation, reduced conflict, better institutions—would mostly follow from that. Not perfectly, but dramatically more than any other single change I can think of.
